newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Samanda says gets okay for timber buys.
newsitem.headline: Samanda says gets okay for timber buys.

text.p: Malaysia's Samanda Holdings Bhd said on Friday it has received regulatory approval for its proposed acquisition of 11 timber companies, but with revisions to the total price it would pay for the assets.

The acquisitions eyed by Samanda will transform the company from a label and adhesive tape maker to a timber industry player with six timber extraction firms and five timber processing companies in eastern Sarawak state.
Samanda is buying the companies from Sarawak-based logging conglomerate WTK Group, which will become a major Samanda shareholder on completion of the proposals.

The Securities Commission approved the acquisitions at a total price of 717.7 million ringgit, lower than an earlier proposal of 839.8 million, the company said in a statement issued by its merchant bankers.
The revision meant that Samanda will issue 48.2 million new shares at 13.15 ringgit each and cash of 83.86 million for the acquisitions.
It had earlier proposed to issue 57.5 million new shares at 13.15 ringgit each and cash of 83.82 million.
Samanda said it plans to seek the commission's approval to pay the 717.7 million ringgit by issuing 49.13 million new shares at 13.15 ringgit and the remainder in cash of 71.61 million ringgit.

The statement said approval for the acquisitions was also conditional on the principal vendors of the 11 companies providing profit guarantees on 100 percent of the pre-tax profit for three financial years after completion of the proposals.
A number of other conditions were attached to the approval. These include one of the companies having to obtain a manufacturing licence and three others their occupational permits.
Samanda said it has also received approval of waiver for its existing major shareholder and the vendors of the 11 companies from making a mandatory general offer for the rest of Samanda shares.

Samanda had said in an earlier statement that the new share issue will make the WTK Group its largest shareholder with a 28.29 percent stake, overtaking Kosa Bahagia Sdn Bhd whose 32.11 percent will be reduced to 16.43 percent.
The proposed acquisitions will still need approval by its shareholders.
Samanda stock was suspended from Thursday, being last traded at 21.10 ringgit.
